description: Retrieve a web page and return its content as markdown (default), text, HTML, a JSON envelope, or a printed PDF. Handles the fetch vs. browser decision, charset decoding, and PDF-to-text for you. Optionally extract structured data with CSS selectors (`extract`) or `autoparse`, return discovered `links`, take a `screenshot`, or scope the DOM with `include_tags`/`exclude_tags`. Each successful call is billed in credits (a failure costs 0). Results are cached by default, and a cache hit is billed like the fetch that stored it (the cache saves time, not credits); set `cache=false` for time-sensitive pages. With the defaults it only reads the page. A `method` other than GET, HEAD or OPTIONS, and the `actions` that click, fill or run scripts on the page, can change state on the target site: set them only when the user asks for that. For markdown, text and HTML it returns `{ content }`. With `format: "json"`, or when `extract`, `autoparse`, `links`, `screenshot` or `network_capture` is set, it returns the JSON envelope: `content`, the site's `status`, `credits`, `engine` (the rendering tier: `fetch`, `js` or `browser`), `warnings` and `data` for extraction. Screenshots come back as image content blocks; each `screenshots` entry in the JSON keeps its metadata and says which block holds it. A PDF comes back as a resource content block, with its size, the rendering tier and the credits in the JSON.

actions.description: Browser steps run in order before capture (render only). Each step is {type, ...fields}. Examples: [{"type":"click","selector":"#load-more"},{"type":"wait_for","selector":".item:nth-child(20)","timeout_ms":5000}] · infinite scroll: [{"type":"scroll","to_bottom":true},{"type":"wait_for","ms":1000}] · login: [{"type":"fill","selector":"#user","value":"me"},{"type":"fill","selector":"#pass","value":"…","secret":true},{"type":"click","selector":"button[type=submit]","wait_for_navigation":true}]. A screenshot step switches the response to the JSON envelope (a FORMAT_COERCED warning says so).

anyOf.description: Click an element. On a checkbox or radio this toggles it (there is no 'set checked'); read its state with evaluate if it matters.

label.description: Name echoed in the response's `actions` and `screenshots`.

on_error.description: fail (default) aborts the workflow; skip records the failure and continues.

selector.description: CSS selector of the element to click.

timeout_ms.description: Budget for this step in ms. The step fails (or is skipped) when it runs out.

until.description: Load state the new document must reach. Default load.

wait_for_navigation.description: The click navigates: finish the step only once the new page has loaded.

anyOf.description: Type a value into an input.

secret.description: A credential: redacted from logs and the request log.

anyOf.description: Wait for a selector to appear, or sleep `ms`.
Wait for a navigation started by the previous step (a click, a form submit, a redirect) to load.

until.description: Load state the new document must reach. Default load.

anyOf.description: Scroll the page: give exactly one of y, to_bottom or selector.

to_bottom.description: Scroll to the bottom repeatedly until the page stops growing (infinite scroll).

y.description: Pixels to scroll down (negative scrolls up).

anyOf.description: Choose option(s) in a <select> by value.

expression.description: JavaScript expression evaluated in the page.

return_value.description: Return the value under `actions` in the response (forces format json).

anyOf.description: Capture the page at this point. The image is returned as an image block; the response becomes the JSON envelope whatever `format` says.

allowed_status_codes.description: Target statuses to treat as success instead of an error (e.g. [404] to capture a not-found page).

autoparse.description: Return the structured data the page publishes about itself (JSON-LD, OpenGraph, Twitter Card, microdata). No selectors; survives redesigns.

block_resources.description: Resource types the browser should not load, e.g. ["fonts","media","images"] (render only). Faster and cheaper.

cache.description: Serve a recent cached result if fresh (on by default). A hit is billed at the same price as the fetch that stored it: the cache saves time, not credits. Set false only when you need live data.

cache_ttl.description: Max age in seconds of a cached copy to accept (0 forces a fresh fetch; capped at 48h). Freshness only: a hit is billed like a fetch.

custom_headers.description: Extra request headers sent to the target, e.g. {"Accept-Language":"de"}.

extract.description: Selector-based extraction: a map of field -> CSS/XPath selector, e.g. {"title":"h1","price":".amount"}. Returns structured `data`. Precise and cheap when you know the page structure.

format.description: Output format. 'markdown' (default) is best for feeding to an LLM; 'html' returns the raw document; 'json' returns a structured envelope; 'pdf' prints the page in a full browser (routed there for you) and returns the file as a resource content block.

impersonate.description: Fetch tier only: present a real browser's TLS/JA3 + HTTP/2 fingerprint to clear passive bot gates. On by default; set false to send a plain client handshake.

include_tags.description: CSS selectors to KEEP (everything else is dropped).

links.description: Also return the page's discovered links as an absolute, de-duplicated list.

main_content_only.description: Strip the page to its main article, dropping nav/footer/aside. Defaults on for markdown.

max_cost.description: Refuse (rather than run) a request that would cost more than this many credits.

method.description: HTTP method sent to the target (default GET; no request body can be sent). Anything but GET, HEAD or OPTIONS can change state on the target site: use it only when the user asks.

mode.description: Routing mode. `auto` lets the platform escalate fetch -> browser as needed, billing only the rung that worked.

network_capture.description: Record the API responses the PAGE fetched while rendering — often cleaner JSON than the DOM. Render only.

urls.description: URL patterns of the page's own requests to record.

original_status.description: Return the target's own HTTP status instead of 200 for a successful scrape.

parse_pdf.description: Turn a PDF target into text/markdown (default true). false refuses PDFs.

proxy.description: Your own proxy URL to egress through. Takes precedence over the pool; no surcharge.

proxy_verify.description: Verify `proxy` is reachable before using it.

render.description: Render with a real browser (executes JavaScript). Use for single-page apps or pages whose content is painted client-side. Costs more than the default fetch tier.

screenshot_fullpage.description: Capture the whole page, not just the viewport.

screenshot_selector.description: Capture only the element matching this CSS selector.

session_id.description: Run inside a session from spicrawl_session_create: same exit IP and browser state (cookies, localStorage) across calls.

wait.description: Milliseconds to wait after load before capturing (render only).

wait_for.description: CSS selector to wait for before capturing (render only).

name: spicrawl_scrape

content.description: The page in the requested format (markdown, text or html); absent for a PDF.

diagnostics.description: Which rendering tiers were tried, after an escalation.

empty_fields.description: `extract` rules that matched nothing: usually a broken selector.

engine.description: Rendering tier that produced the page: fetch, js or browser.

final_url.description: URL after redirects; may be empty.

links.description: The page's links, absolute and de-duplicated, when `links` was set.

network.description: Responses the page fetched, when `network_capture` was set.

pdf.description: Present for format=pdf: the file itself is a resource content block.

attached_as.description: Which resource content block holds the PDF.

not_attached.description: Why the PDF is not attached, and how to get it.

proxy_source.description: Whose exit carried the request: pool, custom or direct.

attached_as.description: Which image content block holds this screenshot.

not_attached.description: Why the image is not attached, and how to get it.

screenshots.description: Metadata of each screenshot; the images are separate image content blocks.

status.description: The target site's HTTP status (not this call's). Anything but 200/404/410 is charged 0.

truncated.description: The target body exceeded the size cap and was cut.

warnings.description: Advisories about the call, e.g. an ignored option.
